headline: High-risk filesystem and network-enabled pairing: Open Interpreter can alter local state while Rasa can relay dialogue to external channels, creating leakage, conflict, and cascading-error risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Open Interpreter reads/writes the local filesystem and clipboard, so attacker-controlled content can reach its instruction stream. Rasa ingests text from chat channels and can pass messages onward. The pair lacks a documented provenance barrier, so prompt-like content can bridge from one agent to the other through shared files or copied outputs.
conditions: IF agent_a writes a file that agent_b later reads as conversational content
IF operator copies agent_a output into a Rasa channel without sanitization
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based handoff between agents
Use separate workspaces for each agent
Add a provenance tag to all transferred text
Require manual review before Rasa ingests agent_a output
requires-engineering: add content filtering at the handoff boundary

B_data_leakage.rationale: Open Interpreter can access the entire local filesystem at the user's privilege and has broad network egress; Rasa can send text/voice through external messaging APIs. If sensitive local files are surfaced into Rasa conversations, data can leave the machine through third-party channels. The pairwise path is plausible from the profiles alone, so uncertainty does not reduce severity.
conditions: IF agent_a reads a sensitive local file and includes its contents in output
IF agent_b forwards that output to Slack, Telegram, Twilio, or another external connector
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of agent_a's workspace
Restrict Rasa connectors to internal test channels
Redact secrets before any handoff
Run agent_a in a separate OS account
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on outbound bot messages

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Open Interpreter has filesystem write and git-state modification, and its concurrency model shares state via the filesystem. Rasa does not expose write capabilities here, but it can still participate in shared mutable workflows through message-driven state. The overlap is enough for conflicting edits or stale state if both touch the same workspace, though not enough for a high rating.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git checkout or shared directory
IF agent_b stores conversation artifacts in a folder agent_a also edits
mitigations: Give each agent a separate directory
Avoid concurrent git operations
Use file locks around shared artifacts
Snapshot the workspace before automation runs
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Open Interpreter can generate code, shell actions, and file edits; Rasa can route text to downstream channels. If Rasa treats Open Interpreter output as authoritative, a mistaken command or fabricated fact can cascade into user-visible messages or operational actions. Because the pair lacks a verification layer by default, the safer choice is the higher severity.
conditions: IF agent_b forwards agent_a output without human verification
IF agent_a produces an incorrect command or factual claim
mitigations: Require human approval before forwarding outputs
Separate drafting from execution roles
Add a verification step in Rasa flows
Limit agent_a to read-only tasks when paired
requires-engineering: implement structured output validation

E_compliance.rationale: Open Interpreter touches anything reachable on the local machine, while Rasa handles text and voice through external connectors. That creates a plausible compliance mismatch for retention, residency, or regulated data handling if sensitive content is routed from local files into chat channels. The profiles do not prove a specific regime breach, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF regulated data is present on the local machine accessed by agent_a
IF that data is then transmitted through an external Rasa connector
mitigations: Block regulated data from agent_a inputs
Use only compliant connectors for Rasa
Document retention settings for each channel
Add a manual compliance review step
requires-engineering: enforce residency and retention controls
